## Trial `configdb-persistence-rhel10__9DAqfRN`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 received routed addresses on both segments with forwarding enabled, a working routed path between node2 and node3 through node1 was demonstrated pre-restart, and the full pre-restart baseline / restart / boot-identity-change / automatic recovery / re-verified connectivity transition was directly observed for node1's restart (and further corroborated by subsequent node2/node3 restarts). The executor also completed the independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes with clear boot-identity changes and recovered state. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found in the command trace.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 given a routed address on each of its two segments (eth1 facing node2, eth2 facing node3)
  - **Why:** cmd-16fb707472a84907 shows eth1 assigned 192.168.1.1/24 and eth2 assigned 192.168.2.1/24 on node1, with IPv4 forwarding enabled globally and per-interface, confirmed via ip -4 addr show. Segment mapping to node2/node3 was independently confirmed via IPv6 link-local neighbor discovery (cmd-9e7f598386c54f37) matching node2/node3 MACs seen in cmd-ef7e0dff0e1c4487/cmd-e963f674e90b4acc.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-16fb707472a84907`, `cmd-9e7f598386c54f37`, `cmd-ef7e0dff0e1c4487`, `cmd-e963f674e90b4acc`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Working routed path between node2 and node3 via node1
  - **Why:** node2 (192.168.1.2/24) and node3 (192.168.2.2/24) were each configured with a static route through node1 via nmcli (cmd-bc10f22bab354a47, cmd-a1cc287eba6348bb), and an end-to-end ping from node2 to node3's routed address succeeded 3/3 before any restart (cmd-1081b1f9737c460a), directly demonstrating a working transit path through node1.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-bc10f22bab354a47`, `cmd-a1cc287eba6348bb`, `cmd-1081b1f9737c460a`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Configuration returns automatically after node1 is restarted, with node2 and node3 reaching each other again once node1 comes back up
  - **Why:** Healthy pre-restart baseline was captured (cmd-7c34690663094b90: boot_id 39fdb9ab..., eth1/eth2 addresses, forwarding sysctls all present) prior to the bounded disruption. node1 was rebooted with an explicit acknowledgement (cmd-3a58e74ba7fe4f5e), and boot_id changed to 329bbe46... confirming an actual reboot occurred (cmd-4026b4e38aff4434). Post-restart, eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls were shown automatically restored with no manual reapplication (cmd-4cebd16060164823), backed by persistent config written to /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1, eth2 and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf (cmd-dec865ec0a754c20). node2->node3 connectivity was re-verified immediately after node1's restart (cmd-ea7da4e48ce64cf4: 2/3 ping replies received, transient loss consistent with post-boot settling) and again after subsequent node2/node3 restarts with clean 3/3 results (cmd-1c67f71310d04e94, cmd-b3ab102c04d940ab), directly demonstrating the full before/disruption/after recovery transition required by this outcome.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7c34690663094b90`, `cmd-3a58e74ba7fe4f5e`, `cmd-4026b4e38aff4434`, `cmd-4cebd16060164823`, `cmd-dec865ec0a754c20`, `cmd-ea7da4e48ce64cf4`, `cmd-1c67f71310d04e94`, `cmd-b3ab102c04d940ab`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. Reviewing every state-changing executor command chronologically: cmd-16fb707472a84907 (node1 address/forwarding assignment), cmd-bc10f22bab354a47 and cmd-a1cc287eba6348bb (node2/node3 nmcli static IP+route), cmd-dec865ec0a754c20 (node1 persistence files), and the three reboot commands (cmd-3a58e74ba7fe4f5e, cmd-82db44a275e74738, cmd-e99189c8f1594f99) each have a clear causal role in satisfying the task's material outcomes or the independently-required provider-wide restart evidence protocol across all three managed nodes. No unnecessary, abandoned, or exploratory mutations were found; all other commands were read-only discovery/verification (ip -br, systemctl cat, nmcli device status, ping, cat). Lifecycle snapshots show no new failed services, no package-manager damage (manager=dpkg/dnf both remained clean pre/post), and no unexpected exposure -- added listening sockets after node1's reboot are the same pre-existing SONiC services (bgpd, zebra, orchagent, eventd, redis) restarting with new PIDs, not new services introduced by the executor. Minor residue of /tmp/reboot.log on node2/node3 is a trivial, low-risk byproduct of the sanctioned reboot mechanism, not a meaningful hygiene concern.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-16fb707472a84907`, `cmd-bc10f22bab354a47`, `cmd-a1cc287eba6348bb`, `cmd-dec865ec0a754c20`, `cmd-3a58e74ba7fe4f5e`, `cmd-82db44a275e74738`, `cmd-e99189c8f1594f99`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node2:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node3:package-health`

### Comments and limitations

- The post-node1-restart ping from node2 to node3 (cmd-ea7da4e48ce64cf4) showed 2/3 replies (33% transient loss) rather than a clean 3/3, though the successful replies still demonstrate recovered connectivity; slightly weaker than the clean results seen after the later node2/node3 restarts.
- Persistence relies on ifupdown2 auto-stanzas under /etc/network/interfaces.d and a sysctl.d drop-in rather than SONiC's native config_db.json mechanism; this was directly verified as working across an actual reboot, but its long-term compatibility with SONiC's config management (e.g., across `config save`/`config reload` operations) was not independently probed.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.950); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
